The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a proposed study by Harvard University aimed at understanding the behavior of aerosol particles in the stratosphere, not a deployment of solar geoengineering. Principal investigator Frank Keutsch and his team presented this concept publicly, emphasizing its role in refining computer models that assess the risks and benefits of solar radiation management. Importantly, SCoPEx was never intended to cool the planet or implement geoengineering practices. 

The planned experiment involved a scientific balloon gondola releasing a minimal amount of calcium carbonate to study aerosol microphysics and light scattering. However, due to concerns about societal implications, the SCoPEx Advisory Committee recommended suspending the project until proper public engagement could occur. As of March 2024, Harvard has announced that the project is no longer being pursued, and the platform will be redirected toward unrelated stratospheric research. 

This highlights the essential need for transparent governance and community involvement in climate interventions, as we strive for justice and accountability in addressing the climate crisis.
